key_objectives: preserve the Arctic as a stable region in which the U.S. homeland remains secure and vital national interests are safeguarded.
enhance domain awareness and communications to better monitor and respond to threats from and through the Arctic.
deepen engagement with Allies and partners, Federal, State, and local authorities; Alaska Native tribes and communities; and industry.
red_lines: PRC's excessive maritime claims along the Northern Sea Route (NSR)
decision_heuristics: if security environment shifts in a way that necessitates response, deploy Joint Force globally at time and place of choosing.
if climate change impacts infrastructure, prioritize investments to sustain critical terrestrial and space-based infrastructure.
escalation_ladder: Enhance intelligence collection and early warning capabilities.
Engage with Allies and partners to strengthen integrated deterrence.
Exercise presence in the Arctic through training and joint operations.
key_quotes: "The United States is an Arctic nation, and the region is critical to the defense of our homeland, the protection of U.S. national sovereignty, and our defense treaty commitments."
"This strategy guides DoD’s efforts to build and sustain this monitor-and-respond approach to the Arctic."
